credentials: PHD 1998 University of Texas at Austin
name: Jean-Luc Thiffeault

ratings.comment: One of the smartest people I have ever met. Someone who enjoys his math and life to the best

one of my best prof. at UW. explains abstract concepts well in lectures. 1HW/2 weeks, though there are ~20 questions.  Very helpful during his OH. There is also a voluntary final review section which really gave a hint to the final exam. Exams are somewhat challenging but not too hard.

Great professor who gives concise, excellent lectures. I did not do the homework but just went to his synchronous OH where he did example problems and studied those before exams. Exams tended to be easier than the homework from Waleffe's textbook.

Making mistakes all the time, so unfamiliar with the materials, reading and copying from the lecture notes all the time. His is really not confident when he is presenting the class, unsure about his own answers or calculations all the time and frequently making mistakes.
Highly recommend staying after lecture to ask him questions; he is great to talk to.
Great professor, especially for math.

His lectures are awesome! He is very passionate about math and care about his students. Homework is very hard (there is a solution manual though). Exams can be as hard as homework. As long as you can do all your homework problems, exams are fine. Another bonus is he allows take-home final!

Gives amazing lectures, but overall a pretty tough class. Take good notes because he covers things very similar to the homework and exam questions. Also, take advantage of the office hours for homework questions. Thiffeault is hilarious though and easy to talk to

OK professor, lectures were good, except I didn't learn much of anything from them. Taught myself from book mostly. If you understand the material, should be easy to get a good grade. Not the best at offering helpful advice. Hmwk isnt bad, should be an easy A, tests give a lot of partial credit and are FROM THE HMWK. Hilarious dude, though.

Easily, the best professor I have had at UW. He really understands the level of students and knows when to repeat things and whether a concept will be easily understood. He also is super funny and keeps the lectures super interesting. Highly would reccomend
Probably the best prof I've had in math, if not at UW.  Makes things really simple.  Most exam questions are right out of the HW/notes.

Teefo is a hilarious French-Canadian who you can tell enjoys the art of mathematics.  His lectures are somewhat entertaining as far as math goes because of his sarcastic and mostly funny political jokes.  However, his exams are SUPER tough.  Clearly his version and a student's version of "applying the math" are completely different.  Study hard
Good professor but a little bit on the hard side.  However, he teaches the class at a high level and occasionaly gives some good advice on how to solve problems.  Jokes around sometimes too.

Professor loves to teach proofs and does not give that many examples in class. Homework and lecture are not mandatory and you only need to attend discussion one day of the week to take weekly quizzes.The tests are crazy hard and are nothing like the homework. He isn't the worst prof, but i would take another one if possible.
Hard Exams
Class is not too bad overall.  Midterms are ridiculously hard, but they are curved.  I got a 61% on one midterm and it ended up being a B.  Pretty fair and likeable guy
tests are hard.  and he don't give practice exams. My TA was horrible too. Nice people, but don't like the class.
He is very good professor. I shall definitely recommend him. He is sound in his understanding of physics and relates them to mathematics that he teaches.

Jean Luc is a fine professor but all he lectures about is proofs - he does very few examples in class... i found no use in attending class - i taught myself out of the book and just tried to do all the homework... his tests are pretty hard because they are usually about four problems totaling 100 points.  i do not recommend him unless you have to!

I guess a lot of the people who are leaving these comments don't really understand what college level math is like. Personally I found the professor to explain things well, and his tests are definitely manageable. Read the book, do the homework, show up to class. It doesn't surprise me there are negative comments - lots of people never showed up.
I've always been good at math and enjoyed it...this class was horrible.

Extremely hard professor.  I'm good at math but still struggled.  Class average on the exams was about 55.  You have to memorize all the proofs.  The curve does treat you nicely though so if you think you're better than most of the class, feel free to take this class.  Otherwise, find an easier professor or take over summer at different school.

He's a nice guy, but the proofs you memorize in first semster! (10 for the final, as well as others for midterms 2&3) He's tricky on the exams, but he likes thomas, and so expect problems derived from there. At the beginning of class he'll tell you everyone can get an A. don't get your hopes up! It's inspiring, but naive. Average, definitely NOTbad

The exam problems can all be found in the book, usually somewhere in the beginning problems. He makes a point to not make the arithmetic too demanding, but know how to factor. There's nothing unfair about the class, and he's a pretty nice guy to boot.

If you want to keep a good GPA DO NOT TAKE CALC WITH TEFO. HE WILL RUIN YOUR GPA. He pretends like he is a nice guy and that his tests are but his final is hellish and his "problems simlar to the book" are nothing of the sort. aka i would never EVER recomend taking calc with him.
